sentences.zh: 乞伏國仁

translations.literal: Qifu Guoren
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Guoren

sentences.zh: 乞伏國仁，隴西鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Qifu Guoren was a man of the Xianbei of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Guoren was a Xianbei of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 在昔有如弗斯、出連、叱盧三部，自漠北南出大陰山，遇一巨蟲于路，狀若神龜，大如陵阜，乃殺馬而祭之，祝曰：「若善神也，便開路；

translations.literal: In former times the three divisions of Rufusi, Chulian, and Chilu came south from beyond the desert, passing out of the Great Yin Mountains, and on the road encountered a huge creature shaped like a divine tortoise, as large as a hill-mound; they killed a horse to sacrifice to it and prayed, saying, "If you are a good spirit, then open the road;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the three clans of Rufusi, Chulian, and Chilu marched south from the northern steppe through the Great Yin Mountains. On the road they met a colossal creature shaped like a sacred tortoise, huge as a hill. They slaughtered a horse as an offering and prayed: "If you are a benevolent spirit, clear our path;

sentences.zh: 惡神也，遂塞不通。

translations.literal: if you are an evil spirit, then block it and we shall not pass."
translations.idiomatic: if you are a malign spirit, let the way be shut and we shall not pass."

sentences.zh: 」俄而不見，乃有一小兒在焉。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward it vanished, and there was a small child present.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment it was gone, and a small boy stood there.

sentences.zh: 時又有乞伏部有老父無子者，請養為子，眾咸許之。

translations.literal: At that time there was also an old man of the Qifu clan who had no son; he asked to adopt the child as his son, and all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: An elder of the Qifu clan who had no son asked to adopt the boy, and the assembly consented.

sentences.zh: 老父欣然自以有所依憑，字之曰紇幹。

translations.literal: The old man was pleased, feeling that he now had someone to rely upon, and gave him the childhood name Heggan.
translations.idiomatic: The old man rejoiced that he finally had someone to lean on, and gave the boy the childhood name Heggan.

sentences.zh: 紇幹者，夏言依倚也。

translations.literal: Heggan means "to lean upon" in the Xia language.
translations.idiomatic: Heggan means "to lean upon" in the Xia tongue.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，驍勇善騎射，彎弓五百斤。

translations.literal: At age ten he was fierce and brave, skilled at riding and archery, and could draw a bow of five hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was already fierce in battle, expert at riding and archery, and could bend a bow rated at five hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 四部服其雄武，推為統主，號之曰乞伏可汗托鐸莫何。

translations.literal: The four divisions submitted to his martial prowess and made him their leader, styling him Qifu Khan Tuoduo Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: All four divisions bowed to his martial prowess and raised him as their chief, calling him Qifu Khan Tuoduo Mohe.

sentences.zh: 托鐸者，言非神非人之稱也。

translations.literal: Tuoduo means a title for one who is neither spirit nor man.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoduo denotes one who is neither spirit nor mortal.

sentences.zh: 其後有祐鄰者，即國仁五世祖也。

translations.literal: Later there was Youlin, who was Guoren's fifth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Youlin, the fifth-generation ancestor of Guoren.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，率戶五千遷于夏緣，部眾稍盛。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Taishi era he led five thousand households to migrate to the Xia frontier, and his following gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taishi era he led five thousand households to the Xia frontier, and his following steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑鹿結七萬餘落，屯于高平川，與祐鄰迭相攻擊。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Lujie had more than seventy thousand households and encamped on the Gaoping River, and he and Youlin attacked each other in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei leader Lujie held more than seventy thousand households on the Gaoping River and traded blows with Youlin in turn.

sentences.zh: 鹿結敗，南奔略陽，祐鄰盡並其眾，固居高平川。

translations.literal: Lujie was defeated and fled south to Lueyang; Youlin absorbed all his followers and held firm on the Gaoping River.
translations.idiomatic: Lujie was beaten and fled south to Lueyang; Youlin absorbed his entire following and entrenched himself on the Gaoping River.

sentences.zh: 祐鄰死，子結權立，徙於牽屯。

translations.literal: When Youlin died, his son Jiequan succeeded and moved to Qiantun.
translations.idiomatic: Youlin died and was succeeded by his son Jiequan, who relocated to Qiantun.

sentences.zh: 結權死，子利那立，擊鮮卑吐賴于烏樹山，討尉遲渴權于大非川，收眾三萬餘落。

translations.literal: When Jiequan died, his son Lina succeeded; he attacked the Xianbei chief Tulai at Wushu Mountain, campaigned against Yuchi Kequan at the Dafei River, and gathered more than thirty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiequan died and his son Lina took the leadership; Lina struck the Xianbei Tulai at Wushu Mountain, campaigned against Yuchi Kequan on the Dafei River, and gathered more than thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 利那死，弟祁埿立。

translations.literal: When Lina died, his younger brother Qilei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Lina died and was succeeded by his younger brother Qilei.

sentences.zh: 祁埿死，利那子述延立。

translations.literal: When Qilei died, Lina's son Shuyan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qilei died and Lina's son Shuyan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 討鮮卑莫侯于苑川，大破之，降其眾二萬餘落，固居苑川。

translations.literal: He campaigned against the Xianbei chief Mohou in Yuanchuan, routed him utterly, and received the submission of more than twenty thousand households, then settled firmly in Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Xianbei Mohou in Yuanchuan, crushed him, and received the submission of more than twenty thousand households before settling firmly in Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 以叔父軻埿為師傅，委以國政，斯引烏埿為左輔將軍，鎮蔡園川，出連高胡為右輔將軍，鎮至便川，叱盧那胡為率義將軍，鎮牽屯山。

translations.literal: He made his uncle Keilei tutor and entrusted him with state affairs; he appointed Siyin Wuqi as Left Assistant General to guard Caiyuan River, Chulian Gaohu as Right Assistant General to guard Zhibian River, and Chilu Nahu as General Who Leads Righteousness to guard Qiantun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his uncle Keilei tutor and entrusted him with government; Siyin Wuqi became Left Assistant General guarding Caiyuan River, Chulian Gaohu Right Assistant General guarding Zhibian River, and Chilu Nahu General Who Leads Righteousness guarding Qiantun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 述延死，子傉大寒立。

translations.literal: When Shuyan died, his son Ludahan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan died and was succeeded by his son Ludahan.

sentences.zh: 會石勒滅劉曜，懼而遷于麥田無孤山。

translations.literal: When Shi Le destroyed Liu Yao, Ludahan, in fear, moved to the Mai Fields and the Solitary Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le destroyed Liu Yao, Ludahan, alarmed, relocated to the Mai Fields and Solitary Mountain.

sentences.zh: 大寒死，子司繁立，始遷於度堅山。

translations.literal: When Ludahan died, his son Sifan succeeded and first moved to Dujian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Ludahan died; his son Sifan succeeded and first moved the seat to Dujian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 尋為苻堅將王統所襲，部眾叛降於統。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was attacked by Fu Jian's general Wang Tong, and his followers rebelled and surrendered to Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was struck by Fu Jian's general Wang Tong; his followers rebelled and went over to Tong.

sentences.zh: 司繁歎謂左右曰：「智不距敵，德不撫眾，劍騎未交而本根已敗，見眾分散，勢亦難全。

translations.literal: Sifan sighed and said to those about him, "Wisdom cannot withstand the enemy, virtue cannot comfort the masses—before swords and horses have even crossed, the root is already lost. Seeing the host scattered, it will be hard to preserve our position.
translations.idiomatic: Sifan sighed to his attendants: "Wisdom cannot hold off the foe, virtue cannot win the people—before blade meets blade our root is already rotten. With the host scattered, our position cannot be saved.

sentences.zh: 若奔諸部，必不我容，吾將為呼韓邪之計矣。

translations.literal: If I flee to the other divisions, they surely will not receive me. I shall adopt the plan of the Hun Shanyu."
translations.idiomatic: If I flee to the other divisions they will not shelter me. I shall do as the Hun Shanyu did."

sentences.zh: 」乃詣統降於堅。

translations.literal: He then went to Tong and surrendered to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Tong and submitted to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅大悅，署為南單于，留之長安。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was greatly pleased and appointed him Southern Shanyu, keeping him at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was delighted, appointed him Southern Shanyu, and kept him at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以司繁叔父吐雷為勇士護軍，撫其部眾。

translations.literal: He made Sifan's uncle Tulei Brave Warriors' Protector of the Army and had him pacify the clan's followers.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Sifan's uncle Tulei Protector of the Army of Brave Warriors to pacify the tribal following.

sentences.zh: 俄而鮮卑勃寒侵斥隴右，堅以司繁為使持節、都督討西胡諸軍事、鎮西將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Before long the Xianbei chief Bohai invaded and pressed Longyou; Fu Jian made Sifan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Campaigns against the Western Hu, and General Who Pacifies the West to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Xianbei chief Bohai raided Longyou; Fu Jian made Sifan bearer of the staff of authority, commander of campaigns against the Western Hu, and General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 勃寒懼而請降，司繁遂鎮勇士川，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Bohai, in fear, requested surrender; Sifan then garrisoned Yongshi River and won great prestige and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai, terrified, sued for peace; Sifan garrisoned Yongshi River and won great authority and goodwill.

sentences.zh: 司繁卒，國仁代鎮，及堅興壽春之役，徵為前將軍，領先鋒騎。

translations.literal: When Sifan died, Guoren replaced him in the garrison; when Fu Jian launched the Shouchun campaign, Guoren was summoned as Forward General and led the vanguard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Sifan died and Guoren took his post; when Fu Jian launched the Shouchun campaign, Guoren was summoned as Forward General to lead the vanguard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 會國仁叔父步頹叛於隴西，堅遣國仁還討之。

translations.literal: At that time Guoren's uncle Bufei rebelled in Longxi, and Fu Jian sent Guoren back to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Guoren's uncle Bufei rebelled in Longxi, and Fu Jian sent Guoren back to put him down.

sentences.zh: 步頹聞而大悅，迎國仁于路。

translations.literal: Bufei, hearing this, was greatly pleased and welcomed Guoren on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Bufei, hearing of it, rejoiced and met Guoren on the road.

sentences.zh: 國仁置酒高會，攘袂大言曰：「苻氏往因趙石之亂，遂妄竊名號，窮兵極武，跨僭八州。

translations.literal: Guoren set out wine for a grand feast, rolled up his sleeves, and spoke loudly: "The Fu clan, riding on the disorder of Zhao and Shi, presumptuously seized the imperial title, exhausted the armies to the utmost, and usurped authority across eight provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren held a great feast, rolled up his sleeves, and declared: "The Fu seized the throne amid the chaos of Zhao and Shi, exhausted every army, and usurped rule across eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 疆宇既寧，宜綏以德，方虛廣威聲，勤心遠略，騷動蒼生，疲弊中國，違天怒人，將何以濟！

translations.literal: Now that the realm is settled they ought to soothe it with virtue; instead they hollow out their prestige, labor at distant schemes, disturb the common people, and weary the Middle Kingdom—defying Heaven and angering men. How can such a course succeed?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is pacified, yet instead of ruling with virtue they squander their prestige on distant schemes, harry the people, and weary the heartland—defying Heaven and enraging men. How can that endure?

sentences.zh: 且物極則虧、禍盈而覆者，天之道也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when things reach their extreme they decline; when misfortune fills up it overturns—such is Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: When things reach their limit they turn; when misfortune overflows it capsizes—that is Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 以吾量之，是役也，難以免矣。

translations.literal: By my reckoning, in this campaign they can hardly escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning, they can hardly escape disaster in this campaign.

sentences.zh: 當與諸君成一方之業。

translations.literal: We should with you all establish a regional enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Let us with you all build a realm of our own.

sentences.zh: 」及堅敗歸，乃招集諸部，有不附者，討而並之，眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian returned defeated, he summoned the various divisions; those who would not submit he campaigned against and absorbed, until his following reached more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian returned in defeat, Guoren rallied the divisions, subdued those who would not follow, and swelled his following to more than one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 及堅為姚萇所殺，國仁謂其豪帥曰：「苻氏以高世之姿而困於烏合之眾，可謂天也。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang, Guoren said to his chieftains, "The Fu clan, with the stature of a lofty age, was brought low by a rabble—one may call that Heaven's doing.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang, Guoren told his chieftains: "The Fu, who bore themselves as lords of a lofty age, were undone by a rabble—that is Heaven's work.

sentences.zh: 夫守常迷運，先達恥之；

translations.literal: To cling to the constant and miss the turning of fortune is what the wise of old were ashamed of;
translations.idiomatic: To cling to routine when fortune turns is what sages of old despised;

sentences.zh: 見機而作，英豪之舉。

translations.literal: to act when one sees the moment is the deed of a hero.
translations.idiomatic: to seize the moment is the act of a true hero.

sentences.zh: 吾雖薄德，藉累世之資，豈可睹時來之運而不作乎！

translations.literal: Though my virtue is slight, I rely on the resources of many generations—how can I watch fortune arrive and not act!"
translations.idiomatic: My virtue may be slight, but I inherit generations of standing—how can I watch fortune arrive and stand idle!"

sentences.zh: 」以孝武自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、領秦、河二州牧，建元曰建義。

translations.literal: He styled himself Xiaowu, Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Governor of Qin and He provinces, and established the era name Jianyi.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Xiaowu, Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Governor of Qin and He provinces, and proclaimed the era Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 以其將乙旃音埿為左相，屋引出支為右相，獨孤匹蹄為左輔，武群勇士為右輔，弟乾歸為上將軍，自余拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He made his generals Yizhan Yingqi Left Chancellor, Wuyin Chuzhi Right Chancellor, Dugu Piti Left Assistant, Wuqun Yongshi Right Assistant, and his younger brother Gangui Upper General; the rest received appointments according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yizhan Yingqi Left Chancellor, Wuyin Chuzhi Right Chancellor, Dugu Piti Left Assistant, Wuqun Yongshi Right Assistant, and his brother Gangui Upper General; the rest received ranks in due order.

sentences.zh: 置武城、武陽、安固、武始、漢陽、天水、略陽、漒川、甘松、匡朋、白馬、苑川十二郡，築勇士城以居之。

translations.literal: He established twelve commanderies—Wucheng, Wuyang, Angu, Wushi, Hanyang, Tianshui, Lueyang, Qiangchuan, Gansong, Kuangpeng, Baima, and Yuanchuan—and built Yongshi City to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: He established twelve commanderies—Wucheng, Wuyang, Angu, Wushi, Hanyang, Tianshui, Lueyang, Qiangchuan, Gansong, Kuangpeng, Baima, and Yuanchuan—and built Yongshi City as his seat.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑匹蘭率眾五千降。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Pilan led five thousand followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Pilan brought five thousand followers to submit.

sentences.zh: 明年，南安秘宜及諸羌虜來擊國仁，四面而至。

translations.literal: The next year, Nan'an Miyi and various Qiang and barbarians came to attack Guoren from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Nan'an Miyi and various Qiang and other tribes attacked Guoren from every side.

sentences.zh: 國仁謂諸將曰：「先人有奪人之心，不可坐待其至。

translations.literal: Guoren said to his generals, "Our forebears had the mind to seize from others; we must not sit and wait for them to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren told his generals: "Our forebears seized when others hesitated; we must not sit idle while the enemy closes in.

sentences.zh: 宜抑威餌敵，羸師以張之，軍法所謂怒我而怠寇也。

translations.literal: We should restrain our prestige and bait the enemy, showing a weak force to inflate them—what the military canon calls making the foe angry while we grow slack."
translations.idiomatic: We should hide our strength and bait them, feigning weakness to swell their pride—what strategists call angering us while the foe grows careless."

sentences.zh: 」於是勒眾五千，襲其不意，大敗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led five thousand men, struck where they did not expect, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He led five thousand men, struck where they did not expect, and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 秘宜奔還南安，尋與其弟莫侯悌率眾三萬餘戶降于國仁，各拜將軍、刺史。

translations.literal: Miyi fled back to Nan'an; soon he and his younger brother Mohou led more than thirty thousand households to surrender to Guoren, and each was appointed general and inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Miyi fled to Nan'an; soon he and his brother Mohou led more than thirty thousand households to submit, and each was made general and inspector.

sentences.zh: 苻登遣使者署國仁使持節、大都督、都督雜夷諸軍事、大將軍、大單于、苑川王。

translations.literal: Fu Deng sent envoys to appoint Guoren Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander, Commander-in-Chief of the Various Yi, Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng sent envoys appointing Guoren bearer of the staff, Grand Commander, commander of the various Yi, Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 國仁率騎三萬襲鮮卑大人密貴、裕苟、提倫等三部於六泉。

translations.literal: Guoren led thirty thousand horsemen to strike the three Xianbei divisions of the great chiefs Migui, Yugou, and Tilun at Liuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren led thirty thousand horsemen against the three Xianbei divisions of the great chiefs Migui, Yugou, and Tilun at Liuquan.

sentences.zh: 高平鮮卑沒奕于、東胡金熙連兵來襲，相遇於渴渾川，大戰敗之，斬級三千，獲馬五千匹。

translations.literal: The Gaoping Xianbei Meiyiyu and the Eastern Hu Jin Xi joined forces to attack; they met on the Kehun River, and after a great battle he defeated them, taking three thousand heads and five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoping Xianbei Meiyiyu and the Eastern Hu Jin Xi joined forces to attack; on the Kehun River he met them in battle, defeated them, and took three thousand heads and five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 沒奕於及熙奔還，三部震懼，率眾迎降。

translations.literal: Meiyiyu and Xi fled back; the three divisions, terrified, led their followers to welcome him and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Meiyiyu and Xi fled; the three divisions, terrified, came in submission.

sentences.zh: 署密貴建義將軍、六泉侯，裕苟建忠將軍、蘭泉侯，提倫建節將軍、鳴泉侯。

translations.literal: He appointed Migui General Who Establishes Righteousness and Marquis of Liuquan, Yugou General Who Establishes Loyalty and Marquis of Lanquan, and Tilun General Who Establishes Discipline and Marquis of Mingquan.
translations.idiomatic: He made Migui General Who Establishes Righteousness and Marquis of Liuquan, Yugou General Who Establishes Loyalty and Marquis of Lanquan, and Tilun General Who Establishes Discipline and Marquis of Mingquan.

sentences.zh: 國仁建威將軍叱盧烏孤跋擁眾叛，保牽屯山。

translations.literal: Guoren's General Who Establishes Prestige Chilu Wugiba led his followers in rebellion and held Qiantun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren's General Who Establishes Prestige, Chilu Wugiba, rebelled with his following and held Qiantun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 國仁率騎七千討之，斬其部將叱羅侯，降者千餘戶。

translations.literal: Guoren led seven thousand horsemen to campaign against him, beheaded his divisional commander Chiluo Hou, and more than a thousand households surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren led seven thousand horsemen against him, beheaded his divisional commander Chiluo Hou, and won the surrender of more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 跋大懼，遂降，復其官位。

translations.literal: Wugiba was greatly afraid and surrendered; Guoren restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wugiba submitted and Guoren restored his office and rank.

sentences.zh: 因討鮮卑越質叱黎于平襄，大破之，獲其子詰歸、弟子復半及部落五千餘人而還。

translations.literal: He then campaigned against the Xianbei chief Yuezhi Chili at Pingxiang, routed him utterly, and returned with Chili's son Jigui, his nephew Fuban, and more than five thousand of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck the Xianbei Yuezhi Chili at Pingxiang, crushed him, and returned with Chili's son Jigui, his nephew Fuban, and more than five thousand of the tribe.

sentences.zh: ，國仁死，在位四年，偽諡宣烈王，廟號烈祖。

translations.literal: Guoren died after four years on the throne; his posthumous title was Prince Xuanlie, and his temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: Guoren died after four years on the throne; his posthumous title was Prince Xuanlie and his temple name Liezu.

sentences.zh: 乞伏-{乾}-歸

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui

sentences.zh: -{乾}-歸，國仁弟也。

translations.literal: Gangui was Guoren's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui was the younger brother of Guoren.

sentences.zh: 雄武英傑，沈雅有度量。

translations.literal: Fierce and martial, a heroic talent, deep and refined, with measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce in battle and heroic in talent, deep-minded and refined, with true breadth of character.

sentences.zh: 國仁之死也，其群臣咸以國仁子公府沖幼，宜立長君，乃推乾歸為大都督、大將軍、大單于、河南王，赦其境內，改元曰太初。

translations.literal: When Guoren died, his ministers all considered Guoren's son Gongfu Chong too young and felt a senior lord should be established; they therefore raised Gangui as Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Henan, amnestied the realm, and changed the era name to Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoren died his ministers judged Gongfu Chong too young and raised Gangui as Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Henan, declared an amnesty, and changed the era to Taichu.

sentences.zh: 立其妻邊氏為王后，以出連乞都為丞相，鎮南將軍、南梁州刺史悌眷為御史大夫，自余封拜各有差。

translations.literal: He made his wife Lady Bian queen, appointed Chulian Qidu chancellor, made General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Southern Liang Tijuan Censor-in-Chief, and the rest received fiefs and appointments according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife Lady Bian queen, appointed Chulian Qidu chancellor and General Who Pacifies the South Tijuan, Governor of Southern Liang, censor-in-chief; the rest received titles in due order.

sentences.zh: 遂遷于金城。

translations.literal: He then moved to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his seat to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: ，苻登遣使署乾歸大將軍、大單于、金城王。

translations.literal: Fu Deng sent envoys to appoint Gangui Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng sent envoys appointing Gangui Grand General, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 南羌獨如率眾七千降之。

translations.literal: The Southern Qiang chief Duru led seven thousand followers to surrender to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Qiang Duru brought seven thousand followers to submit.

sentences.zh: 休官阿敦、侯年二部各擁五千餘落，據牽屯山，為其邊害。

translations.literal: The Xiuguan divisions of Adun and Hounian each held more than five thousand households and occupied Qiantun Mountain, harming his borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiuguan chiefs Adun and Hounian each held more than five thousand households on Qiantun Mountain and raided his borders.

sentences.zh: 乾歸討破之，悉降其眾，於是聲振邊服。

translations.literal: Gangui campaigned against and defeated them, receiving the submission of all their followers; his prestige then shook the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui defeated them and received the submission of all their followers; his name then shook the frontier.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾大人視連遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun great chief Shilian sent envoys bearing local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun great chief Shilian sent envoys with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑豆留䩭、叱豆渾及南丘鹿結並休官曷呼奴、盧水尉地跋並率眾降於乾歸，皆署其官爵。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chiefs Douliuchi, Chidouhun, Nanqiu Lujie, and the Xiuguan chiefs Ehu and the Lushui chief Weidiba all led their followers to surrender to Gangui, and he appointed each to office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Douliuchi, Chidouhun, and Nanqiu Lujie, with the Xiuguan Ehu and the Lushui Weidiba, all brought their followers to submit, and Gangui appointed each to office and rank.

sentences.zh: 隴西太守越質詰歸以平襄叛，自稱建國將軍、右賢王。

translations.literal: The Longxi Administrator Yuezhi Jigui rebelled at Pingxiang and styled himself General Who Establishes the State and Right Worthy Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi Administrator Yuezhi Jigui rebelled at Pingxiang and styled himself General Who Establishes the State and Right Worthy Prince.

sentences.zh: 幹歸擊敗之，詰歸東奔隴山。

translations.literal: Gangui defeated him, and Jigui fled east to Long Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui defeated him and Jigui fled east to Long Mountain.

sentences.zh: 既而擁眾來降，乾歸妻以宗女，署立義將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he led his followers to surrender; Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage and appointed him General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned with his following to submit; Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage and made him General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 苻登將沒奕於遣使結好，以二子為質，請討鮮卑大兜國。

translations.literal: Fu Deng's general Meiyiyu sent envoys seeking alliance, offering his two sons as hostages and requesting a joint campaign against the Xianbei great chief Dadou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's general Meiyiyu sent envoys seeking alliance, offering his two sons as hostages and asking help against the Xianbei great chief Dadou.

sentences.zh: 乾歸乃與沒奕於攻大兜於安陽城，大兜退固鳴蟬堡，乾歸攻陷之，遂還金城。

translations.literal: Gangui joined Meiyiyu in attacking Dadou at Anyang City; Dadou withdrew to hold Mingchan Fortress, which Gangui stormed, then returned to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui joined Meiyiyu against Dadou at Anyang City; Dadou withdrew to Mingchan Fortress, which Gangui took, then returned to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 為呂光弟寶所攻，敗於鳴雀峽，退屯青岸。

translations.literal: He was attacked by Lü Guang's younger brother Bao, defeated at Mingque Gorge, and withdrew to garrison Qing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang's brother Bao attacked him; defeated at Mingque Gorge, he withdrew to Qing'an.

sentences.zh: 寶進追乾歸，乾歸使其將彭奚念斷其歸路，躬貫甲胄，連戰敗之，寶及將士投河死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Bao pressed the pursuit; Gangui had his general Peng Xinian cut off the retreat, then personally donned armor and fought in succession, routing Bao; Bao and his officers and soldiers numbered more than ten thousand dead in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Bao pressed the pursuit; Gangui had Peng Xinian cut the retreat while he himself donned armor and fought until Bao was routed—more than ten thousand of Bao's men drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 苻登遣使署乾歸假黃鉞、大都督隴右河西諸軍事、左丞相、大將軍、河南王，領秦、梁、益、涼、沙五州牧，加九錫之禮。

translations.literal: Fu Deng sent envoys to appoint Gangui acting wielder of the yellow axe, Grand Commander of Longyou and Hexi military affairs, Left Chancellor, Grand General, Prince of Henan, and Governor of Qin, Liang, Yi, Liang, and Sha provinces, with the ritual honors of the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng sent envoys appointing Gangui acting bearer of the yellow axe, commander of Longyou and Hexi, left chancellor, grand general, Prince of Henan, and governor of Qin, Liang, Yi, Liang, and Sha provinces, with the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 時登為姚興所逼，遣使請兵，進封乾歸梁王，命置官司，納其妹東平長公主為梁王后。

translations.literal: At that time Deng was pressed by Yao Xing and sent envoys requesting troops; he advanced Gangui to Prince of Liang and ordered him to establish officials, taking Deng's younger sister the Princess of Dongping as Princess of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng, pressed by Yao Xing, asked for troops, advanced Gangui to Prince of Liang, ordered him to establish a court, and gave him Deng's younger sister, the Princess of Dongping, as princess consort.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遣其前將軍乞伏益州、冠軍翟瑥率騎二萬救之。

translations.literal: Gangui sent his Forward General Qifu Yizhou and Champion Zhai Jin with twenty thousand horsemen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui sent Forward General Qifu Yizhou and Champion Zhai Jin with twenty thousand horsemen to his aid.

sentences.zh: 會登為興所殺，乃還師。

translations.literal: When Deng was killed by Xing, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Deng was killed by Xing before they arrived, and the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊定率步騎四萬伐之。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Ding led forty thousand foot and horse to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Yang Ding led forty thousand foot and horse against him.

sentences.zh: 乾歸謂諸將曰：「楊定以勇虐聚眾，窮兵逞欲。

translations.literal: Gangui said to his generals, "Yang Ding gathers followers through cruelty and violence and exhausts the armies to gratify his desires.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui told his generals: "Yang Ding gathers men through cruelty and exhausts armies to feed his appetites.

sentences.zh: 兵猶火也，不戢，將自焚。

translations.literal: Armies are like fire—if not checked, they will burn themselves up.
translations.idiomatic: Armies are like fire—unchecked, they consume themselves.

sentences.zh: 定之此役，殆天以之資我也。

translations.literal: In this campaign of Ding's, Heaven is likely using him to enrich us."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is likely using Ding's campaign to enrich us."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣其涼州牧乞伏軻殫、秦州牧乞伏益州、立義將軍詰歸距之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent his Governor of Liangzhou Qifu Kechan, Governor of Qinzhou Qifu Yizhou, and General Who Establishes Righteousness Jigui to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Governor of Liangzhou Qifu Kechan, Governor of Qinzhou Qifu Yizhou, and General Who Establishes Righteousness Jigui to meet them.

sentences.zh: 定敗益州于平川，軻殫、詰歸引眾而退。

translations.literal: Ding defeated Yizhou on the Ping River; Kechan and Jigui led their forces in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Ding defeated Yizhou on the Ping River; Kechan and Jigui drew their forces back.

sentences.zh: 翟瑥奮劍諫曰：「吾王以神武之姿，開基隴右，東征西討，靡不席捲，威震秦、梁，聲光巴、漢。

translations.literal: Zhai Jin drew his sword and remonstrated, saying, "Our prince, with divine martial bearing, founded the enterprise in Longyou, campaigning east and west without failing to sweep all before him; his prestige shakes Qin and Liang, his fame resounds through Ba and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Jin drew his sword and protested: "Our prince, with divine martial bearing, founded his realm in Longyou and swept east and west; his prestige shakes Qin and Liang, his fame resounds through Ba and Han.

sentences.zh: 將軍以維城之重，受閫外之寄，宜宣力致命，輔甯家國。

translations.literal: You, General, bear the weight of guarding the capital and have received trust beyond the passes—you ought to exert your strength unto death and assist in securing the state and clan.
translations.idiomatic: You bear the weight of guarding the realm and hold command beyond the passes—you should spend yourself unto death for house and state.

sentences.zh: 秦州雖敗，二軍猶全，奈何不思直救，便逆奔敗，何面目以見王乎！

translations.literal: Though Qinzhou was defeated, the two armies are still intact—how can you not think to rescue them directly, but instead flee before defeat? With what face will you see the prince!
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou fell, yet two armies remain intact—why not turn and save them instead of fleeing before defeat? What face will you show our prince?

sentences.zh: 昔項羽斬慶子以甯楚，胡建戮監軍以成功，將軍之所聞也。

translations.literal: In former times Xiang Yu beheaded Qingzi to secure Chu, and Hu Jian killed the army supervisor to achieve success—things the General has heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu slew Qingzi to secure Chu; Hu Jian executed the army supervisor to win—surely you have heard as much.

sentences.zh: 瑥誠才非古人，敢忘項氏之義乎！

translations.literal: Though Jin's talent is not that of men of old, how dare he forget the righteousness of the Xiang clan!"
translations.idiomatic: My talent is not theirs, yet how dare I forget the Xiang clan's example!"

sentences.zh: 」軻殫曰：「向所以未赴秦州者，未知眾心何如耳。

translations.literal: Kechan said, "The reason I did not go to Qinzhou before was that I did not know the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Kechan said: "I did not march to Qinzhou earlier because I did not know the troops' hearts.

sentences.zh: 敗不相救，軍罰所先，敢自寧乎！

translations.literal: Not to rescue in defeat is what military law puts first—how dare I seek my own ease!"
translations.idiomatic: Military law puts failure to rescue first—how dare I seek my own ease!"

sentences.zh: 」乃率騎赴之。

translations.literal: He then led his horsemen to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his cavalry to their relief.

sentences.zh: 益州、詰歸亦勒眾而進，大敗定，斬定及首虜萬七千級。

translations.literal: Yizhou and Jigui also drove their forces forward, routed Ding utterly, and beheaded Ding along with more than seventeen thousand heads of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou and Jigui advanced as well, crushed Ding, and took Ding's head together with more than seventeen thousand enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 於是盡有隴西、巴西之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he possessed all of Longxi and Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then held all of Longxi and Baxi.

sentences.zh: ，赦其境內殊死以下，署其長子熾磐領尚書令，左長史邊芮為尚書左僕射，右長史秘宜為右僕射，翟瑥為吏部尚書，翟勍為主客尚書，杜宣為兵部尚書，王松壽為民部尚書，樊謙為三公尚書，方弘、麹景為侍中，自余拜授一如魏武、晉文故事。

translations.literal: He amnestied all within his realm below capital punishment, appointed his eldest son Chipan to head the Secretariat, made Left Chief Clerk Bian Rui Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Right Chief Clerk Miyi Right Vice Director, Zhai Jin Minister of Personnel, Zhai Qing Minister of Guests, Du Xuan Minister of War, Wang Songshou Minister of the People, Fan Qian Minister of the Three Excellencies, and Fang Hong and Qu Jing Attendants-in-Ordinary; the rest received appointments according to the precedents of Cao Wu and Jin Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied all below capital punishment, made his eldest son Chipan head the Secretariat, Bian Rui left vice director, Miyi right vice director, Zhai Jin minister of personnel, Zhai Qing minister of guests, Du Xuan minister of war, Wang Songshou minister of the people, Fan Qian minister of the three excellencies, and Fang Hong and Qu Jing attendants-in-ordinary; the rest received ranks after the precedents of Cao Cao and Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 猶稱大單于、大將軍。

translations.literal: He still styled himself Grand Shanyu and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He still bore the titles Grand Shanyu and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 楊定之死也，天水薑乳襲據上邽。

translations.literal: When Yang Ding died, Jiang Ru of Tianshui seized and held Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Ding's death, Tianshui's Jiang Ru seized Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 至是，遣乞伏益州討之。

translations.literal: At this time he sent Qifu Yizhou to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Qifu Yizhou against him.

sentences.zh: 邊芮、王松壽言於乾歸曰：「益州以懿弟之親，屢有戰功，狃於累勝，常有驕色。

translations.literal: Bian Rui and Wang Songshou said to Gangui, "Yizhou, by reason of close kinship with your younger brother, has won repeated victories in battle and, trusting in his string of triumphs, often shows arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Rui and Wang Songshou told Gangui: "Yizhou is your brother's kin and has won battle after battle; grown bold on success, he often shows arrogance.

sentences.zh: 若其遇寇，必將易之。

translations.literal: If he meets the enemy, he will surely treat them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When he meets the foe he is sure to take him lightly.

sentences.zh: 且未宜專任，示有所先。

translations.literal: Moreover, it is not yet fitting to entrust him alone—we should show that someone comes first."
translations.idiomatic: And he should not hold sole command—we must show that another leads."

sentences.zh: 」乾歸曰：「益州驍勇，善禦眾，諸將莫有及之者，但恐其專擅耳。

translations.literal: Gangui said, "Yizhou is fierce and brave, skilled at commanding the masses; among the generals none can match him—I only fear that he may act on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui replied: "Yizhou is fierce and skilled at commanding men; none of the generals equals him—I only fear he may act on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 若以重佐輔之，當無慮也。

translations.literal: If we assist him with weighty deputies, there should be no worry."
translations.idiomatic: With weighty deputies to assist him, there should be no worry."

sentences.zh: 」於是以平北韋虔為長史、散騎常侍務和為司馬。

translations.literal: He therefore made Pingbei Wei Qian chief clerk and Casual Attendant Wu He marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wei Qian of Pingbei chief clerk and Wu He, casual attendant, marshal.

sentences.zh: 至大寒嶺，益州恃勝自矜，不為部陣，命將士解甲遊畋縱飲，令曰：「敢言軍事者斬！

translations.literal: When they reached Dahan Ridge, Yizhou, trusting in victory, grew self-important, made no battle array, and ordered his officers and soldiers to doff their armor and roam hunting and drinking freely, proclaiming, "Whoever speaks of military affairs shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: At Dahan Ridge, Yizhou, drunk on victory, formed no battle line and ordered his men to lay aside armor for hunting and feasting, decreeing: "Whoever speaks of war shall die!"

sentences.zh: 」虔等諫曰：「王以將軍親重，故委以專征之任，庶能摧彼凶醜，以副具瞻。

translations.literal: Qian and the others remonstrated, saying, "The prince, because the general is close and honored, entrusted you with sole command on campaign, hoping you might crush those fierce villains and answer what all look to.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and the others protested: "The prince entrusted you with sole command hoping you would crush these villains and answer what all expect.

sentences.zh: 賊已垂逼，奈何解甲自寬，宴安耽毒，竊為將軍危之。

translations.literal: The enemy is already pressing close—how can you doff your armor and ease yourselves, feasting in the poison of ease? We privately fear for the general's safety."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is upon you—how can you lay aside armor for ease and feast in fatal comfort? We fear for your safety."

sentences.zh: 」益州曰：「乳以烏合之眾，聞吾至，理應遠竄。

translations.literal: Yizhou said, "Ru leads a rabble host; hearing that I have come, by rights he ought to flee far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou said: "Ru leads a rabble; hearing I have come, he ought to flee.

sentences.zh: 今乃與吾決戰者，斯成擒也。

translations.literal: That he now joins battle with me means he is already as good as captured.
translations.idiomatic: That he dares fight me means he is already as good as taken.

sentences.zh: 吾自揣之有方，卿等不足慮也。

translations.literal: I myself have my own plan—you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: I have my own plan—you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 」乳率眾距戰，益州果敗。

translations.literal: Ru led his host to oppose him in battle, and Yizhou was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ru gave battle and Yizhou was defeated.

sentences.zh: 乾歸曰：「孤違蹇叔，以至於此。

translations.literal: Gangui said, "I went against Jian Shu and came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui said: "I went against Jian Shu's counsel and came to this.

sentences.zh: 將士何為，孤之罪也。

translations.literal: What fault is it of the officers and soldiers? The fault is mine alone."
translations.idiomatic: What fault is it of the troops? The fault is mine alone."

sentences.zh: 」皆赦之。

translations.literal: He pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 索虜禿髮如苟，率戶二萬降之，乾歸妻以宗女。

translations.literal: The Suolu chief Tufa Rugou led twenty thousand households to surrender; Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Suolu Tufa Rugou brought twenty thousand households to submit; Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage.

sentences.zh: 呂光率眾十萬將伐乾歸，左輔密貴周、左衛莫者羖羝言於乾歸曰：「光旦夕將至。

translations.literal: Lü Guang led one hundred thousand men to campaign against Gangui; Left Assistant Migui Zhou and Left Guard Moze Gudi said to Gangui, "Guang will arrive within days.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang led one hundred thousand men against Gangui; Left Assistant Migui Zhou and Left Guard Moze Gudi told him: "Guang will arrive within days.

sentences.zh: 陛下以命世雄姿，開業洮罕，克翦群光，威振遐邇，將鼓淳風于東夏，建八百之鴻慶。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with the heroic bearing of one destined for the age, founded the enterprise on the Tao and Han rivers, cut down rival lights, and your prestige shakes the distant realms—you will drum pure winds through the eastern Xia and establish the great blessing of eight hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, born for the age, founded your realm on the Tao and Han, extinguished rival lights, and your name shakes the distant realms—you will bring pure rule to the east and establish an eight-hundred-year blessing.

sentences.zh: 不忍小下屈，與奸豎兢于一時，若機事不捷，非國家利也。

translations.literal: It is unworthy of a lesser lord to bow before a villain and contend with him for a moment; if the opportunity is not seized, it will not benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: A lesser lord should not bow to a villain and contend with him for a moment; if fortune fails, the state suffers.

sentences.zh: 宜遣愛子以退之。

translations.literal: You should send a beloved son to make him withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Send a beloved son to make him withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」乾歸乃稱籓於光，遣子敕勃為質。

translations.literal: Gangui therefore declared himself a vassal of Guang and sent his son Chibo as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui declared himself Guang's vassal and sent his son Chibo as hostage.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，遂誅周等。

translations.literal: Before long he regretted it and put Zhou and the others to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he regretted it and executed Zhou and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 乞伏軻殫與乞伏益州不平，奔于呂光。

translations.literal: Qifu Kechan was at odds with Qifu Yizhou and fled to Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Kechan quarreled with Qifu Yizhou and fled to Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 光又伐之，咸勸其東奔成紀，乾歸不從，謂諸將曰：「昔曹孟德敗袁本初於官渡，陸伯言摧劉玄德于白帝，皆以權略取之，豈在眾乎！

translations.literal: When Guang campaigned against him again, all urged him to flee east to Chengji, but Gangui would not follow and said to his generals, "In former times Cao Mengde defeated Yuan Benchu at Guandu, and Lu Boyan crushed Liu Xuande at Baidi—all took them by stratagem; does it depend on numbers!
translations.idiomatic: When Guang attacked again, all urged flight east to Chengji; Gangui refused and told his generals: "Cao Cao beat Yuan Shao at Guandu and Lu Xun crushed Liu Bei at Baidi—both won by stratagem, not numbers!

sentences.zh: 光雖舉全州之軍，而無經遠之算，不足憚也。

translations.literal: Though Guang has raised the army of the whole province, he has no far-reaching plan and is not to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Guang may field the whole province, but he lacks far sight and is not to be feared.

sentences.zh: 且其精卒盡在呂延，延雖勇而愚，易以奇策制之。

translations.literal: Moreover, his crack troops are all with Lü Yan; though Yan is brave, he is stupid and can easily be controlled by a clever stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: His crack troops are all with Lü Yan—brave but stupid, easily undone by a clever stratagem.

sentences.zh: 延軍若敗，光亦遁還，乘勝追奔，可以得志。

translations.literal: If Yan's army is defeated, Guang too will flee back; pursuing in victory, we can achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat Yan and Guang will flee; pursue in victory and we shall prevail.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸曰：「非所及也。

translations.literal: The host all said, "We cannot match that."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly said: "We cannot match that."

sentences.zh: 」隆安元年，光遣其子纂伐乾歸，使呂延為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longan, Guang sent his son Zuan against Gangui and made Lü Yan vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Longan year 1, Guang sent his son Zuan against Gangui with Lü Yan as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 乾歸泣謂眾曰：「今事勢窮踧，逃命無所，死中求生，正在今日。

translations.literal: Gangui wept and said to the host, "Now our situation is desperate and there is nowhere to flee for life; to seek life in death—today is the day.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui wept to the host: "We are cornered with nowhere to flee; to seek life in death—today is the day.

sentences.zh: 涼軍雖四面而至，然相去遼遠，山河既阻，力不周接，敗其一軍而眾軍自退。

translations.literal: Though the Liang army comes from all four sides, they are far apart; mountains and rivers block them and their strength cannot join—defeat one army and the rest will withdraw of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The Liang host comes from every side, yet they are far apart; mountains and rivers block them and their strength cannot join—break one army and the rest will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」乃縱反間，稱秦王乾歸眾潰，東奔成紀。

translations.literal: He then spread false intelligence, saying that Prince Gangui's host had scattered and fled east to Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: He spread false word that Prince Gangui's host had scattered and fled east to Chengji.

sentences.zh: 延信之，引師輕進，果為乾歸所敗，遂斬之。

translations.literal: Yan believed it, led his army forward lightly, was indeed defeated by Gangui, and was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yan believed it, advanced lightly, was routed by Gangui, and was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤遣使來結和親。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu sent envoys seeking a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu sent envoys to seek a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 使乞伏益州攻克支陽、鸇武、允吾三城，俘獲萬餘人而還。

translations.literal: He sent Qifu Yizhou to storm the three cities of Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu and returned with more than ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qifu Yizhou to take Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu and returned with more than ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 又遣益州與武衛慕容允、冠軍翟瑥率騎二萬伐吐谷渾視羆，至於度周川，大破之。

translations.literal: He also sent Yizhou with Martial Guardian Murong Yun and Champion Zhai Jin with twenty thousand horsemen to campaign against the Tuyuhun chief Shipi; reaching Duzhou River, they routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Yizhou with Murong Yun and Zhai Jin and twenty thousand horsemen against Tuyuhun Shipi; at Duzhou River they crushed him.

sentences.zh: 視羆遁保白蘭山，遣使謝罪，貢其方物，以子宕豈為質。

translations.literal: Shipi fled to hold Bailan Mountain, sent envoys to apologize, presented local products, and offered his son Dangqi as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Shipi fled to Bailan Mountain, sent envoys to apologize, offered tribute, and gave his son Dangqi as hostage.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑疊掘河內率屍五千，自魏降乾歸。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Diejue Henai led five thousand households from Wei to surrender to Gangui.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Diejue Henai brought five thousand households from Wei to submit to Gangui.

sentences.zh: 乾歸所居南景門崩，惡之，遂遷于苑川。

translations.literal: The Nanjing Gate where Gangui dwelt collapsed; taking it as ill omen, he moved to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing Gate of Gangui's residence collapsed; taking it as ill omen, he moved to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 姚興將姚碩德率眾五萬伐之，入自南安峽。

translations.literal: Yao Xing's general Yao Shuode led fifty thousand men to campaign against him, entering by the Nan'an Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's general Yao Shuode led fifty thousand men against him, entering through the Nan'an Gorge.

sentences.zh: 乾歸次於隴西以距碩德。

translations.literal: Gangui encamped at Longxi to oppose Shuode.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui encamped at Longxi to oppose Shuode.

sentences.zh: 興潛師繼發。

translations.literal: Xing secretly sent troops in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xing secretly sent troops in succession.

sentences.zh: 乾歸聞興將到，謂諸將曰：「吾自開建以來，屢摧勍敵，乘機籍算，舉無遺策。

translations.literal: When Gangui heard that Xing was about to arrive, he said to his generals, "Since I founded the enterprise, I have repeatedly crushed fierce foes, seizing opportunity and reckoning by stratagem, and in action never missed a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Xing was coming, Gangui told his generals: "Since I founded my realm I have repeatedly crushed fierce foes by seizing opportunity and stratagem, never missing a plan.

sentences.zh: 今姚興盡中國之師，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: Now Yao Xing has brought the armies of the Middle Kingdom, and his military power is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yao Xing brings the armies of the heartland, and his host is very strong.

sentences.zh: 山川阻狹，無從騎之地，宜引師平川，伺其怠而擊之。

translations.literal: The mountains and rivers are narrow and obstructed, and there is no ground for horsemen—we ought to lead the army onto the open plain and wait for their slackness to strike.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains are narrow and obstruct horsemen—we should draw onto open ground and strike when they slacken.

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，在斯一舉，卿等戮力勉之。

translations.literal: The chance of survival or destruction hangs on this one move—do your utmost, all of you."
translations.idiomatic: Survival or destruction hangs on this one stroke—exert yourselves, all of you."

sentences.zh: 若梟翦姚興，關中之地盡吾有也。

translations.literal: If we behead Yao Xing, all the lands of Guanzhong will be ours."
translations.idiomatic: Behead Yao Xing and all Guanzhong is ours."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣其衛軍慕容允率中軍二萬遷于柏陽，鎮軍羅敦將外軍四萬遷于侯辰穀，乾歸自率輕騎數千候興軍勢。

translations.literal: He therefore sent his Guard General Murong Yun with the central army of twenty thousand to move to Baiyang, Garrison General Luo Dun with the outer army of forty thousand to move to Houchen Valley, and Gangui himself led several thousand light horsemen to observe Xing's military strength.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Yun with twenty thousand of the central army to Baiyang, Luo Dun with forty thousand of the outer army to Houchen Valley, and himself led several thousand light horsemen to scout Xing's strength.

sentences.zh: 俄而大風昏霧，遂與中軍相失，為興追騎所逼，入於外軍。

translations.literal: Before long a great wind arose with dim mist, and he lost contact with the central army; pursued by Xing's cavalry, he entered the outer army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a great wind and dim mist arose; he lost the central army, was pressed by Xing's cavalry, and entered the outer army.

sentences.zh: 旦而交戰，為興所敗。

translations.literal: At dawn they joined battle and were defeated by Xing.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they fought and were defeated by Xing.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遁還苑川，遂走金城，謂諸豪帥曰：「吾才非命世，謬為諸君所推，心存撥亂，而德非時雄，叨竊名器，年逾一紀，負乘致寇，傾喪若斯！

translations.literal: Gangui fled back to Yuanchuan, then ran to Jincheng, and said to the various chieftains, "My talent is not that of one destined for the age; wrongly have you all raised me. My heart was set on putting down disorder, yet my virtue is not the hero of the times—I presumptuously seized the name and instruments, and for more than a decade bore the burden and brought the foe, until ruin came like this!
translations.idiomatic: Gangui fled to Yuanchuan, then to Jincheng, and told the chieftains: "My talent is not for the age; wrongly you raised me. I meant to quell disorder, yet my virtue is not that of a hero of the times—I stole title and regalia for more than a decade until ruin came like this!

sentences.zh: 今人眾已散，勢不得安，吾欲西保允吾，以避其鋒。

translations.literal: Now the host is scattered and our position cannot be secure; I wish to go west and hold Yunwu to avoid their edge.
translations.idiomatic: The host is scattered and we cannot hold; I wish to go west to Yunwu and avoid their edge.

sentences.zh: 若方軌西邁，理難俱濟，卿等宜安土降秦，保全妻子。

translations.literal: If they march west in full strength, it will be hard for us all to survive together—you should settle on your lands and submit to Qin, preserving your wives and children."
translations.idiomatic: If they march west in full strength we cannot all survive—you should settle your lands and submit to Qin, saving your wives and children."

sentences.zh: 」群下咸曰：「昔古公杖策，豳人歸懷；

translations.literal: The host below all said, "In former times Duke Ji of Gu bore his staff, and the people of Bin came to his heart;
translations.idiomatic: The assembly said: "When Duke Ji of Gu bore his staff, the people of Bin came to his heart;

sentences.zh: 玄德南奔，荊、楚繈負。

translations.literal: when Xuande fled south, Jing and Chu carried their children on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: when Xuande fled south, Jing and Chu carried their children on their backs.

sentences.zh: 分岐之感，古人所悲，況臣等義深父子，而有心離背！

translations.literal: The pain of parting is what men of old mourned—how much more we, whose bond is deep as father and son, yet would turn our hearts to desertion!
translations.idiomatic: Parting is what ancients mourned—how much more we, bound deep as father and son, who would desert you!

sentences.zh: 請死生與陛下俱。

translations.literal: We beg to live and die with Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: We beg to live and die with you."

sentences.zh: 」乾歸曰：「自古無不亡之國，廢興命也。

translations.literal: Gangui said, "From antiquity there has never been a state that did not perish; decline and rise are fate.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui said: "From antiquity no state has failed to perish; rise and fall are fate.

sentences.zh: 苟天未亡我，冀興復有期。

translations.literal: If Heaven has not yet destroyed us, there may yet be hope of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven has not destroyed us, restoration may yet come.

sentences.zh: 德之不建，何為俱死！

translations.literal: Since virtue has not been established, why die together!"
translations.idiomatic: Since virtue is not established, why die together!"

sentences.zh: 公等自愛，吾將寄食以終餘年。

translations.literal: Do you each cherish yourselves—I shall live out my years by relying on others for food."
translations.idiomatic: Cherish yourselves—I shall live out my years on others' bounty."

sentences.zh: 」於是大哭而別，乃率騎數百馳至允吾，禿髮利鹿孤遣弟傉檀迎乾歸，處之于晉興。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept greatly and parted; he then led several hundred horsemen in gallop to Yunwu, and Tufa Lilugu sent his younger brother Rutan to welcome Gangui and lodged him at Jinxing.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and parted, led several hundred horsemen to Yunwu, and Tufa Lilugu sent his brother Rutan to welcome him and lodged him at Jinxing.

sentences.zh: 南羌梁戈等遣使招之。

translations.literal: The Southern Qiang chief Liang Ge and others sent envoys to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Qiang Liang Ge and others sent envoys to summon him.

sentences.zh: 乾歸將叛，謀泄，利鹿孤遣弟吐雷屯於捫天嶺。

translations.literal: Gangui was about to rebel, but the plot leaked; Lilugu sent his younger brother Tulei to garrison at Mentian Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui plotted rebellion, but the plot leaked; Lilugu sent his brother Tulei to garrison Mentian Ridge.

sentences.zh: 乾歸懼為利鹿孤所害，謂其子熾磐曰：「吾不能負荷大業，致茲顛覆。

translations.literal: Gangui, fearing that Lilugu would harm him, said to his son Chipan, "I could not bear the great enterprise and brought it to this collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Lilugu would harm him, Gangui told his son Chipan: "I could not bear the great enterprise and brought it to ruin.

sentences.zh: 以利鹿孤義兼姻好，冀存脣齒之援，方乃忘義背親，謀人父子，忌吾威名，勢不全立。

translations.literal: Lilugu's righteousness joins with us through marriage; I hoped for the aid of lip and teeth—yet he forgot righteousness and turned against kin, scheming between father and son, jealous of my prestige and name, so that I cannot stand secure.
translations.idiomatic: Lilugu's bond joins us through marriage; I hoped for mutual aid—yet he forgot righteousness, schemed between father and son, and envies my name so I cannot stand secure.

sentences.zh: 姚興方盛，吾將歸之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing is now ascendant; I shall go over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing is ascendant; I shall go to him.

sentences.zh: 若其俱去，必為追騎所及。

translations.literal: If we all go together, we shall surely be overtaken by pursuing cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: If we all go together, pursuing cavalry will overtake us.

sentences.zh: 今送汝兄弟及汝母為質，彼必不疑。

translations.literal: Now I send you brothers and your mother as hostages—they will surely not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: I send you brothers and your mother as hostages—they will not suspect.

sentences.zh: 吾既在秦，終不害汝。

translations.literal: Once I am in Qin, in the end they will not harm you."
translations.idiomatic: Once I am in Qin, they will not harm you in the end."

sentences.zh: 」於是送熾磐兄弟于西平，乾歸遂奔長安。

translations.literal: He therefore sent Chipan and his brothers to Xiping; Gangui then fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chipan and his brothers to Xiping; Gangui fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 姚興見而大悅，署乾歸持節、都督河南諸軍事、鎮遠將軍、河州刺史、歸義侯，遣乾歸還鎮苑川，盡以部眾配之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, seeing him, was greatly pleased and appointed Gangui Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Henan Military Affairs, General Who Pacifies the Distant, Inspector of Hezhou, and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness; he sent Gangui back to garrison Yuanchuan and assigned him all his tribal following.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing was delighted, appointed Gangui bearer of the staff, commander of Henan, General Who Pacifies the Distant, inspector of Hezhou, and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness, sent him back to Yuanchuan, and assigned him all his following.

sentences.zh: 乾歸既至苑川，以邊芮為長史，王松壽為司馬，公卿大將已下悉降號為偏裨。

translations.literal: When Gangui reached Yuanchuan, he made Bian Rui chief clerk and Wang Songshou marshal; from the three excellencies and great generals downward, all were reduced in rank to divisional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanchuan he made Bian Rui chief clerk and Wang Songshou marshal; from the three excellencies down all were reduced to divisional commanders.

sentences.zh: ，熾磐自西平奔長安，姚興以為振忠將軍、興晉太守。

translations.literal: Chipan fled from Xiping to Chang'an; Yao Xing made him General Who Quells Loyalty and Administrator of Xingjin.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan fled from Xiping to Chang'an; Yao Xing made him General Who Quells Loyalty and administrator of Xingjin.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使者加乾歸散騎常侍、左賢王。

translations.literal: Before long he sent envoys to advance Gangui to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent envoys advancing Gangui to attendant-in-ordinary and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 遣隨興將齊難迎呂隆於河西，討叛羌党龍頭於滋川，攻楊盛將苻帛于皮氏堡，並克之。

translations.literal: He sent the general following Xing, Qi Nan, to welcome Lü Long in Hexi, campaign against the rebel Qiang chief Dang Longtou at Zichuan, and attack Yang Sheng's general Fu Bo at Pishi Fortress—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qi Nan to welcome Lü Long in Hexi, campaign against the rebel Qiang Dang Longtou at Zichuan, and attack Yang Sheng's Fu Bo at Pishi Fortress—all were taken.

sentences.zh: 又破吐谷渾將大孩，俘獲萬餘人而還。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Tuyuhun general Dahai and returned with more than ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Tuyuhun Dahai and returned with more than ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 尋復率眾攻楊盛將楊玉于西陽堡，克之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again led his host to attack Yang Sheng's general Yang Yu at Xiyang Fortress and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again attacked Yang Sheng's Yang Yu at Xiyang Fortress and took it.

sentences.zh: 既而苑川地震裂生毛，狐雉入於寢內，乾歸甚惡之。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanchuan was struck by earthquake; the ground split and grew hair, and foxes and pheasants entered the sleeping quarters—Gangui was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuanchuan suffered earthquake; the ground split and grew hair, and foxes and pheasants entered his bedchamber—Gangui was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 姚興慮乾歸終為西州之患，因其朝也，興留為主客尚書，以熾磐為建武將軍、行西夷校尉，監撫其眾。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, fearing that Gangui would in the end become a worry for the western provinces, detained him when he came to court as Minister of Guests and made Chipan General Who Establishes Martial Might and Acting Commander of the Western Yi, to supervise and pacify the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing, fearing Gangui would become a western menace, detained him at court as minister of guests and made Chipan General Who Establishes Martial Might and acting commander of the western Yi to supervise the masses.

sentences.zh: 熾磐以長安兵亂將始，乃招結諸部二萬七千，築城-{于}-嵻㟍山以據之。

translations.literal: When the troops in Chang'an were about to rise in disorder, Chipan summoned and gathered more than twenty-seven thousand of the various divisions, built a city on Mount Yuqi to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: As Chang'an troops were about to rise in disorder, Chipan gathered more than twenty-seven thousand of the divisions and built a city on Mount Yuqi to hold it.

sentences.zh: 熾磐攻克枹罕，遣使告之，乾歸奔還苑川。

translations.literal: Chipan stormed Fuhan and sent envoys to report it; Gangui fled back to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan took Fuhan and sent word; Gangui fled back to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑悅大堅有眾五千，自龍馬苑降乾歸。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Yuedajian had a following of five thousand and from Longma Park surrendered to Gangui.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei Yuedajian brought five thousand from Longma Park to submit to Gangui.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遂如枹罕，留熾磐鎮之。

translations.literal: Gangui then went to Fuhan and left Chipan to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui went to Fuhan and left Chipan to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 乾歸收眾三萬，遷於度堅山。

translations.literal: Gangui gathered a following of thirty thousand and moved to Dujian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui gathered thirty thousand followers and moved to Dujian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 群下勸乾歸稱王，乾歸以寡弱弗許。

translations.literal: The host below urged Gangui to style himself king; Gangui, because he was few and weak, would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: His followers urged him to take the royal title; Gangui, few and weak, refused.

sentences.zh: 固請曰：「夫道應符曆，雖廢必興；

translations.literal: They pressed him firmly, saying, "The Way responds to the calendar of mandate—though abolished, it must rise again;
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him: "The Way answers the calendar—though abolished it must rise again;

sentences.zh: 圖籙所棄，雖成必敗。

translations.literal: what the charts and registers abandon, though established, must perish.
translations.idiomatic: what the charts abandon, though established, must perish.

sentences.zh: 本初之眾，非不多也，魏武運籌，四州瓦解。

translations.literal: Benchu's host was not small, yet Cao Wu by stratagem made the four provinces collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's host was vast, yet Cao Cao by stratagem made four provinces collapse.

sentences.zh: 尋、邑之兵，非不盛也，世祖龍申，亡新鳥散。

translations.literal: The armies of Xun and Yi were not insignificant, yet when Shizu rose like a dragon, Wang Mang's Xin scattered like birds.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang's armies were vast, yet when Guangwu rose like a dragon, the Xin scattered like birds.

sentences.zh: 固天命不可虛邀，符籙不可妄冀。

translations.literal: Truly Heaven's mandate cannot be sought in vain, nor can charts and registers be hoped for rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate cannot be sought in vain, nor charts hoped for rashly.

sentences.zh: 姚數將終，否極斯泰，乘機撫運，實系聖人。

translations.literal: Yao's number is about to end; when denial reaches its extreme, prosperity comes—seizing the moment to soothe fortune truly belongs to a sage.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's fate is ending; when denial reaches its extreme, prosperity comes—seizing the moment to rule fortune belongs to a sage.

sentences.zh: 今見眾三萬，足可以疆理秦、隴，清蕩洮河。

translations.literal: Now we see a host of thirty thousand—enough to order Qin and Long, clear and sweep the Tao and Han rivers.
translations.idiomatic: We have thirty thousand men—enough to order Qin and Long and sweep the Tao and Han.

sentences.zh: 陛下應運再興，四海鵠望，豈宜固守謙沖，不以社稷為本！

translations.literal: Your Majesty responds to fortune and rises again; the four seas crane their necks in hope—how can you cling to modest humility and not take the altars of state as your foundation!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune raises you again and the realm looks to you—how can you cling to humility and not put the altars of state first!

sentences.zh: 願時即大位，允副群心。

translations.literal: We pray that you take the great position at once and answer the hearts of the host.
translations.idiomatic: Take the throne at once and answer the hearts of all.

sentences.zh: 」乾歸從之。

translations.literal: Gangui followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui consented.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，僭稱秦王，赦其境內，改元更始，置百官，公卿已下皆復本位。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi he presumptuously styled himself Prince of Qin, amnestied the realm, changed the era name to Gengshi, established the hundred offices, and from the three excellencies downward all resumed their former ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 3 he styled himself Prince of Qin, declared an amnesty, changed the era to Gengshi, established offices, and restored ranks from the three excellencies down.

sentences.zh: 遣熾磐討諭薄地延，師次煩於，地延率眾出降，署為尚書，徙其部落于苑川。

translations.literal: He sent Chipan to campaign against and persuade Bodiyan; when the army reached Fanyu, Bodiyan led his host out to surrender and was appointed to the Secretariat; his tribe was moved to Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chipan against Bodiyan; at Fanyu, Bodiyan surrendered and was made secretariat officer; his tribe was moved to Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 又遣隴西羌昌何攻克姚興金城郡，以其驍騎乞伏務和為東金城太守。

translations.literal: He also sent the Longxi Qiang chief Chang He to storm Yao Xing's Jincheng commandery and made the fierce horseman Qifu Wuhe Governor of Eastern Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Longxi Qiang Chang He to take Yao Xing's Jincheng and made the fierce horseman Qifu Wuhe governor of eastern Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 乾歸復都苑川，又攻克興略陽、南安、隴西諸郡，徙二萬五千戶于苑川、枹罕。

translations.literal: Gangui again made Yuanchuan his capital and stormed Xing's commanderies of Lueyang, Nan'an, and Longxi, moving twenty-five thousand households to Yuanchuan and Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui made Yuanchuan his capital again, took Lueyang, Nan'an, and Longxi from Xing, and moved twenty-five thousand households to Yuanchuan and Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 姚興力未能西討，恐更為邊害，遣使署乾歸使持節、散騎常侍、都督隴西嶺北匈奴雜胡諸軍事、征西大將軍、河州牧、大單于、河南王。

translations.literal: Yao Xing lacked the strength to campaign west and, fearing further border harm, sent envoys to appoint Gangui Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of Longxi, Lingbei, Xiongnu, and various Hu military affairs, General Who Campaigns West, Governor of Hezhou, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing could not campaign west and, fearing border raids, appointed Gangui bearer of the staff, attendant-in-ordinary, commander of Longxi and the northern ranges, General Who Campaigns West, governor of Hezhou, Grand Shanyu, and Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 乾歸方圖河右，權宜受之，遂稱籓於興。

translations.literal: Gangui was then plotting the lands west of the Yellow River and, as a temporary measure, accepted; he therefore declared himself Xing's vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui was plotting the Hexi region and accepted for the moment, declaring himself Xing's vassal.

sentences.zh: 遣熾磐與其次子中軍審虔率步騎一萬伐禿髮傉檀，師濟河，敗傉檀太子武台于嶺南，獲牛馬十餘萬而還。

translations.literal: He sent Chipan with his second son, Central Army Shenqian, and ten thousand foot and horse to campaign against Tufa Rutan; crossing the river, they defeated Rutan's heir Wutai south of the ridge and returned with more than one hundred thousand cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chipan and his second son Shenqian with ten thousand foot and horse against Tufa Rutan; crossing the river they defeated Rutan's heir Wutai south of the ridge and returned with more than one hundred thousand cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 又攻克興別將姚龍于伯陽堡，王憬於永洛城，徙四千餘戶于苑川，三千餘戶于譚郊。

translations.literal: He again stormed Xing's detached general Yao Long at Boyang Fortress and Wang Jing at Yongluo City, moving more than four thousand households to Yuanchuan and more than three thousand to Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: He took Xing's Yao Long at Boyang Fortress and Wang Jing at Yongluo City, moving more than four thousand households to Yuanchuan and more than three thousand to Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 乾歸率步騎三萬征西羌彭利發於枹罕，師次於奴葵穀，利發棄其部眾南奔。

translations.literal: Gangui led thirty thousand foot and horse to campaign against the Western Qiang Peng Lifa at Fuhan; the army reached Nu'kui Valley, and Lifa abandoned his following and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui led thirty thousand foot and horse against the Western Qiang Peng Lifa at Fuhan; at Nu'kui Valley, Lifa abandoned his following and fled south.

sentences.zh: 乾歸遣其將公府追及于清水，斬之。

translations.literal: Gangui sent his general Gongfu in pursuit; at Qingshui he caught and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui sent Gongfu in pursuit; at Qingshui he caught and beheaded Lifa.

sentences.zh: 乾歸入枹罕，收羌戶一萬三千。

translations.literal: Gangui entered Fuhan and gathered thirteen thousand Qiang households.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui entered Fuhan and gathered thirteen thousand Qiang households.

sentences.zh: 因率騎二萬討吐谷渾支統阿若干於赤水，大破降之。

translations.literal: He then led twenty thousand horsemen to campaign against the Tuyuhun detached chief Zhitong Aqianyu at Chishui, routed him utterly, and received his submission.
translations.idiomatic: He led twenty thousand horsemen against the Tuyuhun Zhitong Aqianyu at Chishui, crushed him, and received his submission.

sentences.zh: 乾歸畋於五溪，有梟集於其手，甚惡之。

translations.literal: Gangui was hunting at Wuxi when an owl alighted on his hand; he took it as a very ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: While hunting at Wuxi an owl alighted on his hand; he took it as ill omen.

sentences.zh: 六年，為兄子公府所弑，並其諸子十餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was murdered by his nephew Gongfu, together with more than ten of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 his nephew Gongfu murdered him together with more than ten of his sons.

sentences.zh: 公府奔固大夏，熾磐與乾歸弟廣武智達、揚武木奕於討之。

translations.literal: Gongfu fled to hold Gu in Daxia; Chipan with Gangui's younger brother Guangwu Zhida and Yangwu Muyuqiu campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu fled to hold Gu in Daxia; Chipan with Gangui's brothers Zhida and Muyuqiu campaigned against him.

sentences.zh: 公府走，達等追擒於嵻㟍南山，並其四子，轘之于譚郊。

translations.literal: Gongfu fled; Zhida and the others pursued and seized him on Yuqi South Mountain, together with his four sons, and executed them by cart-sundering at Tanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu fled; they caught him on Yuqi South Mountain with his four sons and executed them by cart-sundering at Tanjiao.

sentences.zh: 葬乾歸於枹罕，偽諡武元王，在位二十四年。

translations.literal: They buried Gangui at Fuhan; his posthumous title was Prince Wuyuan; he had reigned twenty-four years.
translations.idiomatic: They buried Gangui at Fuhan with the posthumous title Prince Wuyuan; he had reigned twenty-four years.

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐

translations.literal: Qifu Chipan
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan

sentences.zh: 熾磐，乾歸長子也。

translations.literal: Chipan was Gangui's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan was Gangui's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 性勇果英毅，臨機能斷，權略過人。

translations.literal: By nature he was brave, resolute, heroic, and firm; facing opportunity he could decide, and in stratagem he surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: He was brave, resolute, and firm; facing opportunity he could decide, and in stratagem he surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 初，乾歸為姚興所敗，熾磐質於禿髮利鹿孤。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Gangui was defeated by Yao Xing, Chipan was held as hostage with Tufa Lilugu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gangui was defeated by Yao Xing, Chipan was held hostage with Tufa Lilugu.

sentences.zh: 後自西平逃而降興，興以為振忠將軍、興晉太守，又拜建武將軍、行西夷校尉，留其眾鎮苑川。

translations.literal: Later he fled from Xiping and surrendered to Xing; Xing made him General Who Quells Loyalty and Administrator of Xingjin, then appointed him General Who Establishes Martial Might and Acting Commander of the Western Yi, leaving his host to garrison Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He fled from Xiping to Xing, who made him General Who Quells Loyalty and administrator of Xingjin, then General Who Establishes Martial Might and acting commander of the western Yi, leaving his host at Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 及乾歸返政，復立熾磐為太子，領冠軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Gangui returned to power, he again established Chipan as heir apparent, Champion Grand General, Commander-in-Chief of Central and Outer Armies, and Recorder of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gangui returned to power he made Chipan heir apparent, Champion Grand General, commander of central and outer armies, and recorder of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後乾歸稱籓于姚興，興遣使署熾磐假節、鎮西將軍、左賢王、平昌公，尋進號撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Later, when Gangui declared himself Xing's vassal, Xing sent envoys to appoint Chipan Acting Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Pingchang; soon he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Gangui became Xing's vassal, Xing appointed Chipan acting bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Pingchang, soon advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 乾歸死，，熾磐襲偽位，大赦，改元曰永康。

translations.literal: When Gangui died, Chipan succeeded to the presumptuous throne, declared a great amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gangui died, Chipan succeeded, declared a great amnesty, and changed the era to Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 署翟勍為相國，麹景為御史大夫，段暉為中尉，弟延祚為禁中錄事，樊謙為司直。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhai Qing chancellor of state, Qu Jing censor-in-chief, Duan Hui commandant of justice, his younger brother Yanzuo recorder within the palace, and Fan Qian director of rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhai Qing chancellor, Qu Jing censor-in-chief, Duan Hui commandant of justice, his brother Yanzuo palace recorder, and Fan Qian director of rectitude.

sentences.zh: 罷尚書令、僕射、尚書、六卿、侍中、散騎常侍、黃門郎官，置中左右常侍、侍郎各三人。

translations.literal: He abolished the offices of head of the Secretariat, vice directors, secretaries, the six ministers, attendants-in-ordinary, casual attendants, and gentlemen of the yellow gate, and established left and right regular attendants and gentlemen of the palace, three each.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the secretariat, vice directors, six ministers, attendants, and palace officers, establishing left and right regular attendants and gentlemen of the palace, three each.

sentences.zh: ，遣其龍驤乞伏智達、平東王松壽討吐谷渾樹洛幹於澆河，大破之，獲其將呼那烏提，虜三千餘戶而還。

translations.literal: He sent his Dragon General Qifu Zhida and Prince of Pingdong Wang Songshou to campaign against the Tuyuhun Shuluogan at Jiao River, routed him utterly, captured his general Huna Wuti, and returned with more than three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qifu Zhida and Wang Songshou against Tuyuhun Shuluogan at Jiao River, crushed him, captured Huna Wuti, and returned with more than three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又遣其鎮東曇達與松壽率騎一萬，東討破休官權小郎、呂破胡于白石川，虜其男女萬餘口，進據白石城，休官降者萬餘人。

translations.literal: He also sent his General Who Pacifies the East Tanda with Songshou and ten thousand horsemen east to defeat the Xiuguan chiefs Quan Xiaolang and Lü Pohu at Baishi River, capturing more than ten thousand men and women, advancing to hold Baishi City, with more than ten thousand Xiuguan submitting.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tanda and Songshou with ten thousand horsemen east to defeat Xiuguan Quan Xiaolang and Lü Pohu at Baishi River, taking more than ten thousand captives and holding Baishi City as more than ten thousand Xiuguan submitted.

sentences.zh: 後顯親休官權小成、呂奴迦等叛保白坑，曇達謂將士曰：「昔伯珪憑險，卒有滅宗之禍；

translations.literal: Later the Xianguan Xiuguan chiefs Quan Xiaocheng and Lü Nujia and others rebelled and held Baikeng; Tanda said to his officers and soldiers, "In former times Gongsun Zan relied on peril and in the end met the calamity of extinguishing his clan;
translations.idiomatic: Later Xianguan chiefs Quan Xiaocheng and Lü Nujia rebelled and held Baikeng; Tanda told his troops: "Gongsun Zan relied on peril and in the end his clan was extinguished;

sentences.zh: 韓約肆暴，終受覆族之誅。

translations.literal: Han Yue committed violence and in the end received execution that overturned his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yue committed violence and in the end his whole clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今小成等逆命白坑，宜在除滅。

translations.literal: Now Xiaocheng and the others defy mandate at Baikeng—they ought to be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaocheng and the others defy mandate at Baikeng—they must be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 王者之師，有征無戰，粵爾輿人，戮力勉之！

translations.literal: The army of a true king campaigns without fighting—do your utmost, all you people of the carts!"
translations.idiomatic: A true king's army campaigns without fighting—exert yourselves, all of you!"

sentences.zh: 」眾咸拔劍大呼，於是進攻白坑，斬小成、奴迦及首級四千七百，隴右休官悉降。

translations.literal: The host all drew their swords and shouted; thereupon they advanced on Baikeng, beheaded Xiaocheng and Nujia together with four thousand seven hundred heads, and all the Xiuguan of Longyou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The host drew swords and shouted; they took Baikeng, beheaded Xiaocheng and Nujia with four thousand seven hundred heads, and all Longyou Xiuguan submitted.

sentences.zh: 遣安北烏地延、冠軍翟紹討吐谷渾別統句旁於泣勤川，大破之，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He sent Pacifier of the North Wudiyan and Champion Zhai Shao to campaign against the Tuyuhun detached chief Jubang at Qiqin River, routed him utterly, and captured a very great number.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wudiyan and Zhai Shao against Tuyuhun Jubang at Qiqin River, crushed him, and took a great many captives.

sentences.zh: 熾磐率諸將討吐谷渾別統支旁于長柳川，掘達於渴渾川，皆破之，前後俘獲男女二萬八千。

translations.literal: Chipan led his generals to campaign against the Tuyuhun detached chief Zhibang at Changliu River and Jueda at Kehun River—both were defeated; in all they captured twenty-eight thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan led his generals against Tuyuhun Zhibang at Changliu River and Jueda at Kehun River—both were crushed—and captured twenty-eight thousand men and women in all.

sentences.zh: 僭立十年，有雲五色，起于南山，熾磐以為己瑞，大悅，謂群臣曰：「吾今年應有所定，王業成矣！

translations.literal: In the tenth year of his presumptuous reign, five-colored clouds arose from the southern mountains; Chipan took them as his own omen, was greatly pleased, and said to his ministers, "This year I ought to achieve something definite—the royal enterprise is accomplished!"
translations.idiomatic: In his tenth year five-colored clouds rose from the southern mountains; Chipan took them as his omen and told his ministers: "This year my royal enterprise is accomplished!"

sentences.zh: 」於是繕甲整兵，以待四方之隙。

translations.literal: He then repaired armor and marshaled troops, waiting for openings in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired armor and marshaled troops, waiting for openings in every quarter.

sentences.zh: 聞禿髮辱檀西征乙弗，投劍而起曰：「可以行矣！

translations.literal: Hearing that Tufa Rutan was campaigning west against the Yifu, he cast aside his sword and rose, saying, "We can act!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Tufa Rutan was campaigning west against the Yifu, he cast aside his sword and cried: "Now we can act!"

sentences.zh: 」率步騎二萬襲樂都。

translations.literal: He led twenty thousand foot and horse in a surprise strike on Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: He led twenty thousand foot and horse in a surprise strike on Ledu.
